name: GlobalStiffnessTimeStepper
description: An engine assigning the time-step as a fraction of the minimum eigen-period in the problem. The derivation is detailed in the chapter on DEM formulation <DEMSimulations>. The viscEl option enables to evaluate the timestep in a similar way for the visco-elastic contact law...

attributes.name: defaultDt
attributes.description: used as the initial value of the timestep (especially useful in the first steps when no contact exist). If negative, it will be defined by

attributes.name: maxDt
attributes.description: if positive, used as max value of the timestep whatever the computed value

attributes.name: timestepSafetyCoefficient
attributes.description: safety factor between the minimum eigen-period and the final assigned dt (less than 1)

attributes.name: densityScaling
attributes.description: (auto-updated) don't modify this value if you don't plan to modify the scaling factor manually for some bodies. In most cases, it is enough to set

attributes.name: targetDt
attributes.description: if densityScaling is active, this value will be used as the simulation timestep and the scaling will use this value of dt as the target value. The value of targetDt is arbitrary and should have no effect in the result in general. However if some bodies have imposed velocities, for instance, they will move more or less per each step depending on this value.

attributes.name: viscEl
attributes.description: To use with ViscElPhys. if True, evaluate separetly the minimum eigen-period in the problem considering only the elastic contribution on one hand (spring only), and only the viscous contribution on the other hand (dashpot only). Take then the minimum of the two and use the safety coefficient timestepSafetyCoefficient to take into account the possible coupling between the two contribution.

attributes.name: dead
attributes.description: If true, this engine will not run at all; can be used for making an engine temporarily deactivated and only resurrect it at a later point.

attributes.name: ompThreads
attributes.description: Number of threads to be used in the engine. If ompThreads<0 (default), the number will be typically OMP_NUM_THREADS or the number N defined by 'yade -jN' (this behavior can depend on the engine though). This attribute will only affect engines whose code includes openMP parallel regions (e.g. InteractionLoop). This attribute is mostly useful for experiments or when combining ParallelEngine with engines that run parallel regions, resulting in nested OMP loops with different number of threads at each level.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Textual label for this object; must be valid python identifier, you can refer to it directly from python.

attributes.name: execTime
attributes.description: Cumulative time in nanoseconds this Engine took to run (only used if O.timingEnabled == True).

attributes.name: execCount
attributes.description: Cumulative count this engine was run (only used if O.timingEnabled == True).

attributes.name: timingDeltas
attributes.description: Detailed information about timing inside the Engine itself. Empty unless enabled in the source code and O.timingEnabled == True.

methods.name: updateAttrs
methods.description: Update object attributes from given dictionary
